title: Fund Governance and Compliance for Managers and Service Providers
summary: A ten-module programme giving fund managers and service providers the practical tools to meet fund rules and supervisory expectations across the fund lifecycle.
intro: This training programme equips fund managers, fund boards and service providers to meet fund manager and fund product rules in practice, from delegation and valuation to liquidity, costs, private markets and tokenised funds.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give fund managers and their service providers a practical understanding of the rules and supervisory expectations that govern funds and the people who run them. Participants leave able to strengthen governance, delegation, valuation and liquidity arrangements, and to see their fund range the way a supervisor does.
sections.What It Covers: Fund manager and fund product rules, delegation and substance, the depositary and trustee interface, valuation, liquidity risk management, costs, value and disclosure, conflicts of interest, private markets and retail access, tokenised funds, and engaging with the supervisor.
Intended Audience: Compliance, risk and legal staff at fund managers and investment managers
Fund administrators, depositaries, trustees, transfer agents and other service providers
Fund board directors, conducting officers and senior managers overseeing fund ranges
Learning Objectives: Explain how fund manager and fund product rules apply across the fund lifecycle
Assess delegation, substance and the oversight of service providers
Design sound valuation and liquidity risk management frameworks
Evaluate costs, value, disclosure and conflicts in investors' interests
Identify the risks of private markets, retail access and tokenised funds
Engage effectively with the supervisor and agree a compliance action plan
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, group exercises and practical checklists, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's fund range and role.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of the investment funds sector is helpful. No prior knowledge of specific fund rules is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes (2018)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
FSB, Revised Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Liquidity Mismatch in Open-Ended Funds (2023)
IOSCO, Examination of Governance for Collective Investment Schemes (2006–2007)

modules.title: The Fund Regulatory Framework
modules.summary: How fund manager and fund product rules fit together, the main fund types and structures, and the responsibilities of the manager, the fund's governing body and its service providers.
objectives: Explain how fund manager and fund product rules interact
Distinguish retail, professional and private fund structures and their regulatory treatment
Identify the roles and responsibilities of each party in the fund ecosystem
syllabus: Fund manager authorisation versus fund product approval
Retail, professional and private funds: structures and investor protections
Fund boards, managers, administrators, depositaries and distributors
The IOSCO Objectives and Principles and international fund standards

modules.title: Delegation, Substance and Oversight
modules.summary: How managers delegate portfolio management, risk management and administration while retaining the substance, expertise and oversight that supervisors expect.
objectives: Assess whether the manager retains sufficient substance and decision-making
Design due diligence and ongoing oversight of delegates
Identify letter-box risks and how supervisors test for them
syllabus: Delegation models and the limits on what can be delegated
Substance: people, expertise, resources and decision-making
Delegate due diligence, service levels and ongoing monitoring
Intragroup and cross-border delegation

modules.title: The Depositary and Trustee Interface
modules.summary: The independent role of the depositary or trustee in safekeeping and oversight, and how managers and service providers build an effective working relationship with it.
objectives: Explain the safekeeping, cash monitoring and oversight duties of the depositary or trustee
Manage the information flows and escalations between manager and depositary
Respond effectively to depositary challenges and breach reports
syllabus: Safekeeping, record-keeping and asset verification
Cash flow monitoring and oversight of dealing, valuation and investment limits
Service agreements, escalation and breach reporting
Independence and conflicts in the depositary relationship

modules.title: Valuation
modules.summary: How to design and govern a valuation framework that produces fair and reliable values, particularly for hard-to-value and illiquid assets.
objectives: Design a valuation policy and governance framework
Assess valuation approaches for illiquid and complex assets
Identify valuation conflicts and errors and respond to them
syllabus: Valuation policy, committee and functional independence
Pricing sources, models and fair value adjustments
Illiquid assets, private markets and valuation uncertainty
Pricing errors, investor compensation and NAV suspensions

modules.title: Liquidity Risk Management
modules.summary: How managers align fund liquidity with redemption terms, use stress testing and liquidity management tools, and respond when liquidity comes under pressure.
objectives: Align portfolio liquidity with dealing frequency and investor profile
Design liquidity stress testing and monitoring
Select and govern liquidity management tools
syllabus: Liquidity mismatch and lessons from fund suspensions
Liquidity stress testing for assets and liabilities
Liquidity management tools: swing pricing, anti-dilution levies, gates and suspensions
FSB and IOSCO recommendations on fund liquidity

modules.title: Costs, Value and Disclosure
modules.summary: How firms assess whether funds deliver value for the costs charged, and how to disclose costs, risks and objectives in a way that is fair, clear and not misleading.
objectives: Assess whether a fund delivers value relative to its costs
Ensure cost and charges disclosure is complete and accurate
Evaluate the clarity and accuracy of fund documents and marketing
syllabus: Fee structures, undue costs and value assessments
Cost and charges disclosure, including transaction costs
Prospectus, key information documents and periodic reporting
Marketing communications and sustainability-related claims

modules.title: Conflicts of Interest and Fund Governance
modules.summary: How conflicts arise across the fund lifecycle and how managers, boards and service providers identify, manage and evidence their resolution in investors' interests.
objectives: Identify conflicts across portfolio management, dealing and service provision
Design conflicts registers, policies and controls
Assess the role of the fund board and independent oversight in managing conflicts
syllabus: Common conflicts: allocation, cross-trades, related parties and fees
Inducements, soft commissions and intragroup arrangements
Conflicts policies, registers and disclosure
Board challenge and independent directors

modules.title: Private Markets and Retail Access
modules.summary: The growth of private equity, private credit and infrastructure funds, the move to give retail investors access, and the governance, valuation and liquidity challenges this brings.
objectives: Explain the main private market strategies and fund structures
Assess the risks of offering private market exposure to retail investors
Design product governance and distribution controls for semi-liquid funds
syllabus: Private equity, private credit, real estate and infrastructure funds
Semi-liquid and evergreen structures for wider investor access
Target market, suitability and distribution controls
Leverage, valuation and liquidity in private markets

modules.title: Tokenised Funds and Technology
modules.summary: How tokenisation, distributed ledgers and new technology are changing fund issuance, dealing and servicing, and the regulatory and operational questions this raises.
objectives: Explain how tokenised fund units are issued, held and transferred
Assess custody, record-keeping and settlement risks in tokenised models
Identify how existing fund rules apply to new technology
syllabus: Tokenised fund units and on-chain registers
Custody, transfer agency and settlement on distributed ledgers
Tokenised money market funds as collateral and settlement assets
Technology, AI and operational resilience in fund servicing

modules.title: Engaging with the Supervisor
modules.summary: Brings the programme together around supervisory engagement: applications, ongoing reporting, thematic reviews and inspections, closing with a compliance action plan.
objectives: Prepare effective fund and manager applications and notifications
Respond well to supervisory reviews, information requests and inspections
Produce a fund governance and compliance action plan
syllabus: Applications, notifications and regulatory reporting
Thematic reviews, inspections and common supervisory findings
Breach reporting, remediation and investor redress
Workshop: seeing the fund range the way a supervisor does

related.title: Private Markets and Private Credit for Managers
related.summary: An eight-module advanced programme giving private markets managers and service providers the tools to manage valuation, leverage, liquidity and conflicts risks and meet supervisory expectations.

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition

related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.

related.title: Fund Regulation Country Briefings
related.summary: Eleven country webinar briefings on fund vehicles, regulators, authorisation, distribution and recent developments in leading European, offshore and Asia Pacific fund markets.

related.title: International Fund Regulation: Global and Regional Briefings
related.summary: A ten-module webinar series mapping international, EU and Asia Pacific fund regulation and how cross-border fund distribution, management and investment are regulated.

related.title: Introduction to Investment Funds: From Launch to Wind-Down
related.summary: A fourteen-module foundation programme taking new funds professionals and supervisors through every stage of an investment fund, from structure and regulation to operations and wind-down.
